rate_distortion_conclusion: A shared operator with intermediate width m<17408 is a narrow bottleneck of a 17408-wide MLP shared across layers. Its function quality degrades smoothly with narrowness: m=6144 -> ~0.59-0.95, and matching q3's 0.337 requires m~10000-12000, at which point the operator's active bytes approach q3's own -- NO Pareto win. There is no m giving BOTH q3-quality AND a materially smaller active-byte footprint. The earlier 'beats q3 at 0.37' was a degenerate-corpus + methodology artifact (audit-refuted).

physics_context: Token active ~11.7 GB, bandwidth ~471 GB/s -> ~40 TPS bandwidth ceiling; measured ~30 TPS. 100 TPS needs <=~4.7 GB active. MLP is ~7 GB (68% of GEMV). Only cutting the MLP to near-zero active hits 100 TPS, and that requires a coherent ~40MB MLP operator, which the evidence says does not exist. Matches prior campaign memory: '100 TPS unreachable by density at all' on this model class.
